The GDR was not a “proxy” of the Soviet Union. It had a different political system from the Soviet Union not least that it had several legal political parties representing different social strata. And the planned economy had far more input at factory level. The VEBs (Volkseigene Betriebe) — people-owned enterprises where most East Germans worked had trade union representation with formal rights to negotiate implementation of plans, influence working conditions and challenge management over safety, discipline, and welfare through workers meetings. So it’s simply not accurate to say all “eastern bloc nations at resources, capital and labour allocated from the top.” This isn’t to ignore the failings of these political systems but let’s be accurate.
